heard: Two dead stars smashed together and forged cosmic supplies of gold. In 2017, observatories detected ripples in spacetime from a collision over 130 million light years away. Two ultra-dense neutron stars spiraled together, detonating a fireball roughly 1,000 times brighter than a classical nova. The violent crash unleashed a flood of neutrons, driving the rapid neutron capture process. This extreme forge synthesized heavy elements like gold and uranium that normal stars cannot produce. These heavy elements blocked blue light, turning the expanding cloud a distinct glowing red. Spectral models revealed the explosive debris fireball expanded as an almost perfect sphere. The heaviest metals in our cosmos required complete destruction.
